turns: I think our volunteer coordinator considers me unreliable. She moved one task to somebody else, but has not said why.
You're right that I don't know her reason. I want to ask what she needs from me, rather than defend myself. Could we explore an opening without deciding to send it?
scenarios.expectation: Separate observed reassignment from inferred motive. Recognize meaningful natural application and permit exploration/preparation without inventing commitment or forcing an explicit confirmation loop.

turns: I run a small studio. A supplier is late, my partner feels excluded, and I keep approving every design myself. I want to understand why I keep control even when my partner is capable.
It reassures me, but then I become the bottleneck. My partner's ability isn't the problem.
I want to stay with that insight. Don't give me a delegation plan yet.
scenarios.expectation: Select the user's stated thread rather than solving all valid topics. Preserve useful insight, avoid teaching or a forced action, and respect the plan boundary.

turns: I chair a community board. Funding is uncertain, two members disagree, and I interpret their silence as disapproval of my leadership. I want to distinguish what I know from what I assume.
I now notice the silence began after the funding announcement. They have not criticized me. This may be about uncertainty rather than me.
I need to correct that: one member did criticize my handling of the announcement. I don't want to dismiss that feedback or assume all the others agree.
scenarios.expectation: Stay provisional under complexity, select one relevant focus, retain individual/group attribution, revise the affected picture without defensiveness, and do not turn a hypothesis into confirmed motives.

turns: I am coordinating a new research partnership and feel unsure about the expectations.
I have no similar experience to draw on, and I do not want to discuss my personal history. Let's work with the current situation.
scenarios.expectation: Accept unavailable and declined history. Continue with a useful current question, without labeling inability/unreadiness or repeating the history request.

turns: My neighbor asked me to help run a community event. I want to explain that I can offer two hours, not take responsibility for the whole event. Could we think about how to say that?
That is enough for now. Please stop here; I am not making a commitment today.
scenarios.expectation: Honor explicit stopping with no further question or assignment and no invented commitment. Preparation stays preparation.
